title: Add logging + redaction for public benchmark artifacts
author: Rina Kobayashi
commits: benchmark-export: add public artifact redaction pass
logging: add structured export logs w/ safe fields only
tests: add redaction fixtures + golden outputs
body:
Context: As part of the latency/$ benchmark report work, we now export versioned JSON/CSV artifacts for ingestion by the marketing site (see #4867). During security review we noticed we were including several fields that are safe for internal analysis but should not be published (trace IDs, fleet/node identifiers, internal request IDs, and some runner-environment metadata). While none of these are customer secrets, they increase operational leakage and can complicate legal/compliance review. This PR adds an explicit redaction + allowlist layer for the public artifact export path, plus safer logging to ensure we don’t accidentally print sensitive values during export.

What changed: (1) Implemented a deterministic redaction pass for the public export pipeline. The exporter now constructs an explicit allowlist schema ("public_result_v1") and drops/normalizes any fields not in the schema. For fields that are useful for reproducibility but risky when too granular, we transform rather than remove: region is kept (e.g., "us-east"), but AZ and node/fleet IDs are removed; model revision hashes are truncated to 8 chars; runner image digest is omitted. (2) Added token/ID scrubbing for freeform strings using a conservative regex-based sanitizer. This targets patterns we’ve seen leak into manifests and error strings (e.g., "Authorization: Bearer ...", "x-redwood-request-id=...", "traceparent=..."). Scrubbing is best-effort and is applied only in the public export path; internal artifacts remain unchanged. (3) Updated structured logging during export to log only safe summary fields (schema_version, run_id, model, region, prompt_set, concurrency, counts) and explicitly never log raw headers, request identifiers, or full manifest blobs. (4) Added tests with fixtures (unredacted sample -> redacted expected) and a golden schema assertion that will fail CI if new fields are added to public artifacts without a deliberate schema change. (5) Added a new "PUBLIC_ARTIFACT_REVIEW" checklist doc and a step in README for anyone running exports locally/CI. The checklist includes: verify schema version, run redaction tests, sample-check that no internal IDs appear, and confirm the export logs show "redaction_applied=true".

Redaction rules (high-level): removed: runner.env.*, runner.host*, runner.instance_id, runner.node_id, runner.fleet_id, tracing.trace_id/span_id/traceparent, request_id, internal_job_id, raw_error_context, retry_debug. transformed: model_revision -> short hash, timestamps -> rounded to seconds (kept), region -> kept, az -> dropped, sdk_user_agent -> kept only for internal artifacts (dropped in public).

Example (before -> after): before: {"run_id":"run_2025-06-22_17-02-11","region":"eu-west","az":"eu-west-1c","runner":{"node_id":"gpu-node-17c3","image_digest":"sha256:..."},"tracing":{"traceparent":"00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01"},"error":"upstream 429 for request_id=req_01J..."} after: {"schema_version":"public_result_v1","run_id":"run_2025-06-22_17-02-11","region":"eu-west","model":"...","metrics":{...},"warnings":["error_message_redacted"]}

Why allowlist vs blacklist: We started with blacklist but it was too easy to miss new fields added by unrelated changes (e.g., new tracing metadata). Allowlist + schema versioning forces an explicit decision when fields are added.

Test plan: - unit: python -m pytest export/public_artifacts/__tests__ - unit: schema stability test (fails if unexpected key appears) - local smoke: ran export on 2 recent manifests (1 passing run, 1 with injected error strings containing request_id) and confirmed public JSON contains no runner/node/tracing keys - verified logs: grep -E "traceparent|Bearer|request_id|node_id" in exporter stdout is empty

Rollout/compat: This changes only the public artifact export outputs. Internal artifacts + analysis codepaths remain intact. The web ingestion should not break because it is already reading a small subset of keys; however, to be safe, schema_version is now required and added to output. Follow-up: once this merges, we should pin the marketing site ingestion to public_result_v1 explicitly and reject unknown versions (tracked in ENG-18566).

Notes for reviewers: Please focus on (a) whether the allowlist includes everything we need for reproducibility in the report, (b) whether the sanitizer patterns are too broad (risk removing meaningful error info), and (c) whether any other fields should be considered sensitive operational data.

Screenshots/log excerpts: Included in comments below (export log sample showing redaction stats + fixture diff).
review_conversation: Naomi Feldman (Security): Please ensure we are not writing the unredacted fixture to CI artifacts; even if it’s synthetic, we don’t want a pattern of checking in anything that looks like tokens/headers. Also the sanitizer regex currently matches any 32+ char base64-ish string; that might redact model revision IDs unintentionally.

Rina Kobayashi (Author): Good call. Updated fixtures to use obvious placeholders ("BEARER_TOKEN_EXAMPLE") and added a comment that it’s synthetic. Also tightened sanitizer to look for explicit prefixes (Bearer, Authorization:, x-redwood-*, traceparent=) rather than generic base64 length.
Mei Lin (Data): Can we keep prompt_set name + prompt_set_version in public artifacts? We’ll need it for the methodology appendix and to debug user questions about workload mix.
Rina Kobayashi (Author): Added prompt_set (name + version) to allowlist and included it in export logs. Confirmed it doesn’t leak any prompt content (we never export prompts).
Jonas Weber (Perf/Evals): We should keep concurrency + prefill/decode token sizes. Those drive most of the variance questions we expect post-launch.
Rina Kobayashi (Author): Added concurrency, input_tokens, output_tokens, and the workload label to the public schema. Also rounded timestamps but kept run_duration_sec + sample counts.

Sofia Mendes (Legal): Please avoid the term "scrub tokens" in docs; use "redact sensitive identifiers" and explicitly note that this does not include customer content because customer content is not present in benchmark artifacts.

Rina Kobayashi (Author): Updated docs wording per request and added a note: benchmark artifacts never include customer prompts or customer-provided data; this redaction is about internal operational identifiers.
